summary: A quiet 21-message week while she was in LA shooting - and the quiet is the story, because the one thing that did happen is the thing last week's report warned would happen. On Sep 14 at 20:30 she posted a screenshot and wrote 'Ur chatters have to stop doing this please' / 'He doesn't want old content'. That is the ELEVENTH time she has issued the no-old-content rule since Jun 12, the first repeat since Teddi came back at $200+/video, and it lands 11 days after she pre-emptively re-issued the rule on Sep 3 and got no reply. Fred did not see it for 13 hours and only answered at 09:33 on Sep 15 after Mayson escalated at 01:35 - the ninth @fspitfire escalation on this account. His answer was his weakest yet: another verbal briefing plus a tool excuse, 'it appears as not sent before on Infloww so we'll get them to do this in the mean time'. The chatter he promised to remove on Jul 24 is still unnamed 56 days later, and there is still no mechanical purchase-history check. Beyond that one exchange, NOTHING moved for a third consecutive window: the Aug 29 lost-spender sequence is 20 days unanswered, the two Aug 26 instructions are 23 days unanswered, the $100/min shower custom is 38 days idle, the Adam West red set is 30 days unsold, the $750 whipped-cream fan has been waiting 18 days for a 'couple days' answer, the $192 ledger gap is 24 days unreconciled, and TIKTOK IS NOW 31 DAYS DEAD WITH THREE CONSECUTIVE WINDOWS OF TOTAL SILENCE from every single person including her. The Instagram Reels account she discovered on Sep 10 has still never received a file - 98 days - and the login she promised that day has not arrived: on Sep 16 she wrote 'I still need to get u the insta login... need to figure it out', which is a client saying she is stuck, and Mayson replied 'Okay thanks' and 'And the facebook'. Payments were the genuine bright spot AND the new risk. Stephski fixed four flagged process misses in one cycle - the day-before withdrawal reminder came back on Sep 14, the Sep 1-14 invoice went out exactly on cadence on Sep 15, the template no longer re-introduces 'Stephanie' to a four-month client, and wire details were surfaced. But the same message announced a SIXTH change to ALTR's receiving details ('Please note a slight name change to the account') and added a service-suspension line to a client with a flawless four-month record: 'we appreciate you paying within the next 7 days to avoid any pausing in work!'. Her reaction was immediate - 'Wait a different Zelle again?' - and the owner had to step in personally at 01:33 to calm it. Meanwhile the Aug 15-31 invoice issued Sep 3 has STILL never been confirmed received, 15 days on, so two invoices are now stacked on top of the unreconciled $192 against a $500/day sending cap nobody has done the arithmetic on.
